source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Read one increment of an elementary Itô integral. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: On any cell of an adapted dyadic elementary integrand's own grid, its completed Itô integral increment agrees almost surely with the cell coefficient times the corresponding Brownian increment.
assumptions: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The integrand is a dyadic elementary adapted process with its bounded, left-endpoint measurable cell coefficients.

The scalar driver is Brownian under μ relative to the given filtration. It is the driver for both the completed integral and the increment on the right. The chosen cell belongs to the elementary process's own grid.
source_evidence.boundary: The equality is almost sure for each chosen cell of the elementary process's own deterministic grid.

steps.title: Identify the endpoint values

steps.text: Expand the difference of the elementary sums. Earlier cells are complete at both endpoints. Later cells contribute zero at both endpoints. The selected cell gives the displayed coefficient times the driver increment.
